name: DutyLens
one_liner: Upload your import catalog and get every SKU's correct HTS code with cited CBP precedent, true landed cost with all stacked tariffs, and an alert the moment a rate changes.
summary: Small US importers ($50k–$50M) lost the $800 de minimis exemption (Aug 2025) and now need a correct 10-digit HTS code, stacked duty rate and 'reasonable care' documentation on every SKU. Per Christensen's Jobs-to-be-Done, the job is 'tell me my true landed cost and don't let CBP fine me.' Wedge is a Hormozi Grand Slam Offer: a $1,500 Tariff Exposure Audit delivered in 3–5 days, converting to $99–499/mo SKU monitoring (Ramanujam's willingness-to-pay-first pricing). Moat is a RAG index (Lewis et al. 2020) over 220k CBP CROSS rulings, the HTS schedule and Federal Register 301/232/122 actions. Distribution per Weinberg & Mares' Bullseye: Shopify App Store plus FBA seller communities. First revenue 10–20 days.

name: WageLens
one_liner: Type in your project's county and craft, get the legally correct prevailing-wage rate, and auto-generate the weekly WH-347 certified payroll report.
summary: Small specialty subcontractors on federal/state prevailing-wage jobs must map every worker to the right Davis-Bacon county-and-craft rate weekly and file WH-347; misclassification is the most common violation ($13,508 per violation, back wages, three-year debarment), and a 2023 DOL rule pushes prime-contractor liability downstream. Deep-and-narrow per Paul Graham: lookup plus auto-filled WH-347, not a payroll suite. $79–99/mo sub tier, $299/mo GC tier, transparently priced against incumbents' quote-gated $175–2,000/mo (April Dunford: position against the competitive alternative). Moat is a versioned archive of SAM.gov wage determinations by county/craft/date plus SF-1444 conformance precedent. SAM.gov and USASpending award feeds give a warm outbound list; weekly payroll deadlines force a close inside 30 days.

name: StateReady
one_liner: Never let a technician's license, CE, bond or insurance lapse again — and get a step-by-step playbook for getting licensed in your next state.
summary: Multi-state trade contractors (HVAC/electrical/plumbing, 5–100 techs) must track per-state license, CE, bond and insurance renewals and decode reciprocity when entering a new state; a lapse halts permit pulls and can void job insurance. Hormozi-style offer ladder: free 'license lapse risk audit' → $149–599/mo tracking → $750–1,500 one-time state-expansion report. Willingness to pay is observed, not asserted (Fitzpatrick's Mom Test standard): LicensedTrades.com already sells $199–1,199/mo and concierge filers charge per state. Moat is a normalized 50-state × trade licensing/CE/reciprocity database scraped from board PDFs — the scattered data NASCLA only publishes as static directories. Beachhead per Moore: PE-backed trade roll-ups actively entering new states. Revenue in ~30 days.

name: ScopeIQ
one_liner: Tell us your state and your procedures, and get a cited answer on who can inject what, under whose supervision, and which ownership structure is legal — plus the paperwork.
summary: Med spa owners and nurse injectors face 50 different CPOM/ownership, delegation and supervision regimes that change yearly (California's 2026 MSO rewrite); errors risk cease-and-desist orders, six-figure fines and criminal exposure. AmSpa's 3,000+ members paying $395–845/yr and attorneys charging $3,500–10,000 per structuring question are Mom-Test-grade evidence of money already spent. Entry offer is a $499–999 one-time state launch compliance report — fast cash, no procurement — upsold to $99–499/mo multi-state monitoring, per Ramanujam's willingness-to-pay-first ladder. Moat: a continuously updated, cited 50-state scope/CPOM/delegation database with change alerts, which static $197 PDF kits structurally cannot match. Sell into owner Facebook groups and MSOs signing new-state leases; first revenue inside 30 days.

name: StayLegal
one_liner: Give us your rental's address and we file your short-term-rental permit for you, then keep it renewed as the city's rules change.
summary: Over 100 US cities require STR permits ($50–925 fees, inspections, renewals) spread across municipal PDFs, with fines up to $5,000 per stay while cities buy Granicus enforcement software to hunt unpermitted listings. Existing tools only inform; per Hormozi's value equation, actually filing collapses effort and time delay, which is where the price lives: $149–249 one-time per property plus $19–29/mo monitoring, validated against Avalara MyLodgeTax's $27/mo/property + $299 setup for the tax slice alone. Moat: a scraped, structured ordinance-and-form database per jurisdiction that compounds city by city. Delivery starts as Ries' concierge MVP, sold into r/AirBnBHosts, BiggerPockets and host Facebook groups; paying customer in 2–3 weeks.

name: Reinstate
one_liner: Paste your Amazon or Walmart suspension notice and get a submission-ready Plan of Action in minutes, drafted from the policies and appeal patterns that actually get sellers reinstated.
summary: Suspended marketplace sellers are in maximum-urgency, maximum-willingness-to-pay mode; Riverbend Consulting services 400+ appeals monthly at $1,000+ with 10,000 sellers served and sells monitoring subscriptions — Mom Test evidence of money already changing hands, not stated interest. Reinstate drafts a customized Plan of Action from the notice: $39–79/mo monitoring plus a $299–499 rush human-reviewed appeal. Market pull is visible daily in Seller Central forums, satisfying Andreessen's 'only thing that matters' test. Moat: a structured corpus of policy text, suspension reason codes and anonymized winning appeal patterns, retrieved per Lewis et al.'s RAG. Distribution is Weinberg & Mares' community channel — answer live 'just got suspended' posts with a free draft. Revenue in days.

name: Recoup
one_liner: We read the bills your counterparties send you, find the overcharges and underpayments, and take a cut of the money we get back.
summary: Multi-unit tenants receive CAM reconciliation statements where roughly 40% contain errors and audits recover 15–20% of annual CAM, yet the contractual audit window closes in 90 days–12 months. Recoup ingests lease plus statement, flags overcharges and drafts the dispute, sold at the industry-norm 30–50% contingency so there is no budget approval step — Hormozi's risk reversal maximizing perceived likelihood of achievement. The same engine extends to insurance carrier commission statements, PBM remittances and ocean detention/demurrage invoices; CAM is the Moore beachhead. Moat: an accumulating structured dataset of which landlords and property managers systematically over-bill which expense categories. A free first-pass audit of three statements converts inside 30 days.

name: Certly
one_liner: An AI compliance clerk that reads every vendor's certificate of insurance, checks it against your contract requirements, and chases the renewal before it lapses.
summary: Small property managers (50–500 units) and GCs (20–150 subs) verify every vendor's ACORD 25 certificate against contract limits, additional-insured status and waiver language by hand in spreadsheets; gaps surface only at claim time. TrustLayer and myCOI (16 years, 45M+ documents processed) prove the category is funded and monetized, but both are demo-gated enterprise — a classic down-market self-serve wedge per Poyar/OpenView's PLG research and Christensen's low-end disruption. $99–299/mo self-serve, tiered by certificates tracked. Moat: extraction patterns across hundreds of non-standard carrier PDF layouts plus state- and lease-specific requirement templates, improving with every document. A free COI audit reliably surfaces an already-expired policy, and that finding is the close. Revenue under 30 days.
